parties.name: BC NDP
parties.leaderNote: Premier during the campaign; resigned as leader on election night
parties.status: Campaign launch priorities; further details are being announced.

items.summary: Support workers and businesses affected by tariffs and expand trade into markets beyond the United States.

points.text: Expand trade beyond the United States and support tariff-affected workers and businesses.
Double skilled trades training by 2028–29 to prepare BC residents for jobs in major projects.
Target $200 billion in major project investment by 2035.
Use the Manufacturing Jobs Fund, Rural Economic Diversification and Infrastructure Program, Integrated Marketplace and BuyBC to support businesses and market diversification.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: Ongoing program and investment goals; $200 billion refers to major project investment, not a provincial spending allocation.

items.summary: Keep family costs down and build the housing and infrastructure BC needs.

points.text: Continue policies aimed at reducing household costs through housing supply, child care, public auto insurance and electricity rates.
Continue child care fee reductions and ICBC rate freezes.
Maintain property transfer tax relief for first-time homebuyers.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: The party presents these as ongoing policies and projects, alongside its record in government. The reviewed material does not set out a new across-the-board cash benefit or a new tax-cut amount.

items.summary: Recruit more health workers and strengthen health care and public services.

points.text: Continue recruiting and training doctors, nurses and other health workers, including recruitment from the United States.
Continue work on 24 new or expanded hospitals, including nine already completed, and new community and First Nations primary care centres.
Continue training physicians through SFU’s Surrey medical school and expanding nurse practitioner-led care.
Continue developing 37 long-term care homes.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: The party presents these as ongoing policies and projects, alongside its record in government.

items.summary: Choose Canadian goods where possible and maintain the US alcohol ban until a fair deal for forest workers.

points.text: Keep US alcohol off shelves until a fair deal is reached for BC forest workers.
Coordinate with the federal government and other provinces on Canadian countermeasures.
Expand BuyBC beyond agriculture to help more local businesses find markets.
Buy Canadian goods and maintain public procurement restrictions on US suppliers.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: The party presents these as ongoing policies and projects, alongside its record in government.

items.summary: Continue housing supply reforms, short-term rental restrictions and measures against speculation.

points.text: Continue zoning reforms intended to permit more middle-class housing across BC.
Maintain short-term rental restrictions and the Speculation and Vacancy Tax.
Use the $1 billion Growing Communities Fund to support local infrastructure, including transportation, recreation and child care facilities.
Maintain zoning changes intended to allow 300,000 additional homes.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: Ongoing housing policies. The 300,000-home figure describes capacity enabled by zoning changes.

items.summary: Expand access to treatment, youth mental health services and care for people in severe crisis.

points.text: Continue expanding the Road to Recovery program and Access Central for assessment and entry into treatment.
Open 15 additional Foundry centres for young people, alongside the 20 centres already operating.
Continue building involuntary care capacity for people in severe crisis and supportive housing for people who need it.
Maintain free opioid agonist treatment medications and access to free or low-cost counselling.

sources.label: Action for You: ongoing plans and party record

items.note: The party presents these as ongoing policies and projects, alongside its record in government.

parties.name: Conservative Party of BC
parties.status: Selected commitments from the party’s campaign plan.

items.summary: Raise the personal income tax exemption to $32,000 and pledge no tax increases during its term.

points.text: Raise the basic personal income tax exemption from $13,216 to $32,000.
Target annual income tax savings of $1,000 per working person and $2,000 per average couple, according to the party’s estimates.
Commit to no tax increases throughout its term in government.

items.note: Savings are party estimates and depend on taxable income.

items.summary: Maintain health spending and invest in doctors and nurses to keep emergency rooms and maternity wards open.

points.text: Create a $50 million emergency fund and support rural medical practices at risk of closure.
Recruit and retain more doctors and nurses while protecting current health funding and keeping the system universal and publicly funded.
Train more doctors in BC, bring back Canadians who studied medicine abroad and accelerate international credential recognition.
Launch an expert commission within the first 100 days to identify approaches from other public health systems and reduce wait times.
Keep covered care accessible with a health card.

items.summary: Expand natural gas and LNG production, with growth targets for 2032 and 2035.

points.text: Double natural gas production by 2032 and triple it by 2035, as stated in the detailed announcement.
Accelerate project approvals and reduce regulatory barriers to new energy development.
Build the power supply and infrastructure needed for expansion.
Promote First Nations partnerships and ownership in new projects.

items.note: The plan overview refers to LNG, while the detailed announcement calls the targets natural gas production; the sources use different descriptions.

items.summary: Repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).

points.text: Repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
Pursue economic reconciliation through development projects built in partnership with First Nations.

items.note: The party describes financial and social success through these partnerships but does not specify a replacement legislative framework in this announcement.

items.summary: Expand police and court capacity, treatment services and mandatory care interventions.

points.text: Add 250 police officers through expanded Police Academy capacity, plus 500 RCMP officers and 150 civilian staff over five years.
Hire 50 Crown prosecutors and work with Ottawa on funding 20 additional trial judges, alongside more sheriff and court capacity.
Expand psychiatric services, crisis response and residential treatment; amend the Mental Health Act to connect people with mandatory care.
End safer supply, expand naloxone access and prohibit illegal drug use in hospitals, shelters and publicly funded supportive housing.
Publish measures of repeat offending, court delays, treatment access and long-term recovery.

items.summary: Expand insurance choice and compensation rights for serious injuries while retaining ICBC.

points.text: Introduce a hybrid insurance approach giving people seriously injured by reckless drivers rights to compensation and legal representation.
Preserve ICBC as a public insurance option while expanding consumer choice where competition could improve price and service.
Protect access to treatment and rehabilitation, with legal fee limits intended to control litigation costs.
Require clear service standards and public reporting.

items.summary: Buy firefighting aircraft and invest in fuel reduction, prescribed burns and early detection.

points.text: Procure firefighting aircraft, including waterbombers.
Reduce forest fuels around communities and simplify prescribed-burn approvals without lowering safety standards.
Allow qualified firefighting resources to respond more quickly during emergencies.
Create a dedicated fund for early detection and prevention technology, with preparation intended for the next fire season.

items.summary: Remove SOGI from schools while committing to student safety.

points.text: Remove SOGI from schools.
Maintain safe places for children to learn.

items.note: The reviewed statement does not provide replacement curriculum details or a rollout timetable.

parties.name: BC Green Party
parties.leaderNote: Leader; newly elected in Saanich North and the Islands
parties.status: Published priorities; the party says its full platform is coming soon.

items.summary: Build and protect 26,000 permanently affordable non-market homes annually and limit rent increases between tenants.

points.text: Build and protect 26,000 permanently affordable non-market homes each year.
Simplify and accelerate construction of all forms of housing.
Introduce vacancy control so rent limits stay with the unit when tenants change.

items.note: The annual target includes new construction and protection of existing affordable homes.

items.summary: Make public transit frequent, fast and free.

points.text: Eliminate transit fares and increase service speed and frequency.
Use proposed wealth and corporate revenue measures to help finance public transit.

items.note: The priorities page does not yet provide individual route plans, service-frequency targets or a rollout schedule.

items.summary: Build community health centres in every region and cover mental health care through the public system.

points.text: Build team-based community health centres in every region, with long-term patient support.
Complete implementation of safe nurse-to-patient ratios.
Provide publicly covered mental health care and direct public health dollars to public care.
Invest in harm reduction and voluntary addiction treatment.

items.summary: Stop new fossil fuel development and introduce proportional representation legislation within the first 100 days.

points.text: Stop new fossil fuel development and support clean energy and home retrofits.
Fully fund old-growth logging deferrals with compensation for First Nations and forestry communities.
Support selective logging, value-added industries and mining-law reforms for renewable-energy resources.
Introduce proportional representation legislation within the first 100 days.

items.note: The 100-day deadline applies to introducing legislation.

items.summary: Make solar and home batteries easier to approve and finance, including options for apartment residents.

points.text: Restore one-for-one net metering for homes and small businesses until their solar generation supplies about 5% of provincial electricity demand.
Create one provincial application portal covering incentives, municipal permits, electrical approval and BC Hydro connections.
Use certified equipment and pre-approved designs to speed up standard rooftop solar and battery installations.
Create a legal and technical pathway for plug-in balcony solar, including systems usable by renters and apartment residents.
Offer low-cost BC Hydro financing repaid through electricity bills, with early repayment allowed without a penalty.

items.note: This proposal is from the economic vision, which the party distinguishes from its forthcoming full platform.

items.summary: Tax extreme wealth to fund public services and strengthen provincial finances.

points.text: Introduce a one-time progressive tax on net wealth above $50 million, followed by an annual wealth tax.
The proposed one-time rates are 5% on $50 million+, 10% on $100 million+ and 20% on $1 billion+; annual rates are 2%, 3% and 5% at those thresholds.
The party estimates $22.2 billion in one-time revenue and about $5.4 billion annually; these are its modelling estimates.
Strengthen valuation, reporting and enforcement to limit avoidance and use revenue for services, infrastructure and provincial finances.

items.summary: Protect commercial tenants and give communities more tools to keep businesses locally rooted.

points.text: Limit commercial rent increases during leases, at renewal and between tenants, supported by a provincial rent registry.
Begin by collecting rent and lease data, then phase in the protections across BC.
Give municipalities authority to tax vacant commercial property, with exemptions for genuine redevelopment and insufficient demand.
Create purchase opportunities for commercial tenants, First Nations, cooperatives and community organizations.

items.summary: Expand affordable child care and raise income supports and worker protections.

points.text: Restart expansion of $10-a-day child care and work toward universal access with fair pay for early childhood educators.
Raise social and disability assistance above the poverty line, index payments to inflation and end clawbacks.
Increase the minimum wage toward a living wage and expand opportunities for workers to organize through sectoral bargaining.

otherParties.status: Platform in development. The party lists affordability, health care, economic growth, fiscal responsibility, sustainability and Indigenous relations as policy areas, but has not published specific commitments on this page.

otherParties.name: Christian Heritage Party of BC

items.summary: Repeal DRIPA and replace it with a reconciliation framework that respects constitutional and treaty rights and includes materially affected parties.

points.text: Repeal DRIPA and review laws, agreements, land measures and commitments introduced under it.
Retain constitutional Aboriginal and treaty rights and existing binding obligations.
Bring First Nations and other materially affected communities, landowners, workers and businesses into the replacement framework.
Define responsibilities, land and resource arrangements, revenue sharing and measurable outcomes.

items.summary: Direct more resources to frontline care and establish independent oversight of medical assistance in dying.

points.text: Reduce administrative costs and direct resources to frontline, mental health, home and palliative care.
Create a MAID oversight body independent of the Ministry of Health and health authorities.
Authorize case audits and complaint investigations, with public reporting on safeguards, consent and access to alternative care.
Protect conscience rights for health professionals and institutions.

items.summary: Use suitable public land, long-term leases and faster approvals to lower housing costs.

points.text: Identify serviceable Crown and other public land near communities for housing.
Use long-term leases, partnerships and carefully structured land releases to lower land costs.
Fast-track approvals where infrastructure supports development while maintaining environmental and property protections.
Publish project targets for homes, affordability, final cost, completion and taxpayer contributions.

items.summary: Stop using SOGI 123 in schools and focus teaching on core academic subjects and practical skills.

points.text: Stop use of SOGI 123 and gender-identity teaching described in its platform.
Give parents visibility into teaching materials and sensitive subjects.
Focus instruction on literacy, mathematics, science, history, civics and practical skills.
Protect students from bullying and mistreatment.

items.summary: Expand detox, residential treatment and recovery services, with medically overseen involuntary admission when legal criteria are met.

points.text: Expand detox, residential treatment, psychiatric care and long-term recovery.
Connect crisis care to supportive housing, employment and independence.
Use involuntary admission when the legal threshold is met, with medical oversight and regular review.
Coordinate police, prosecutors, corrections and treatment services.

items.summary: Review provincial spending and require public reporting of budgets, deadlines and results.

points.text: Require major programs to have a budget, deadline and measurable outcome.
Review spending ministry by ministry, including consulting contracts, administrative growth and duplication.
Publish promised and actual spending, results, missed deadlines and corrective action.
Correct, replace or end programs that repeatedly fail to achieve their objectives.

items.summary: Eliminate income tax on earnings below $50,000 and increase the contribution from corporations and wealthy taxpayers.

points.text: End provincial income tax on earnings below $50,000.
Reverse the 2001 tax reductions for wealthy people and corporations.
Fund housing, education, transit and social services through progressive provincial taxation.

items.summary: Build 100,000 new or renovated public housing units, tie rent controls to units and limit rents to 20% of household income.

points.text: Build 100,000 new or renovated social and low-income public housing units.
Tie rent controls to units and legislate rents at no more than 20% of household income.
Prohibit renovictions, demovictions and economic or no-fault evictions.
Use homes vacant for more than two years as social housing and stop encampment clearing until permanent housing is available.

Reduce the work week to 32 hours without reducing pay.
Extend sectoral bargaining, picketing rights and protections for domestic, agricultural and migrant workers.
Strengthen card-check certification, anti-scab legislation and penalties for union-busting.

sources.label: Communist Party of BC — Our Platform (2026)

items.summary: Make public transit free and create an accessible province-wide bus system.

Create and enforce transit-only lanes in major cities.
Keep transit publicly owned and under democratic control.

Prioritize renewable energy and conservation.
Retrain fossil-fuel workers into other jobs at union wages.
Make polluting corporations pay for reversing environmental damage.

Increase hospital beds, train doctors and nurses and fund hospitals to prevent emergency closures.
End privatization and contracting out of health services.
Offer incentives for students from remote communities to return there to practise.

otherParties.name: Libertarian

items.summary: Simplify development regulations and expand opportunities for housing supply.

points.text: Make the Agricultural Land Commission advisory and allow non-arable land to leave the Agricultural Land Reserve, with a one-time levy when such land is sold or developed.
Simplify municipal zoning into broader industrial, commercial, mixed-use, housing and recreational categories.
Reduce or eliminate property transfer tax and end the School Tax, speculation, empty-home and home-flipping taxes.
Ease rent controls, revise tenancy rules to encourage rental supply and pause the Step Code.
Phase out rental assistance programs.

items.note: These policy articles are linked by the 2026 platform; their original publication dates are in 2024.

items.summary: End ICBC’s monopoly on basic auto insurance.

points.text: Allow competing providers for basic and optional auto insurance.
Convert ICBC’s insurance business into a member-owned cooperative, with members able to choose another insurer.
Repeal no-fault legislation and restore access to pain-and-suffering compensation and legal representation.
Return licensing and registration responsibilities to provincial and regional offices.
Sell the North Vancouver head office property and use proceeds for liabilities and provincial debt.

items.note: These policy articles are linked by the 2026 platform; their original publication dates are in 2024.

items.summary: Cut government spending, return savings to taxpayers and reduce provincial debt. End PST on private vehicle sales.

points.text: Raise the personal income tax exemption to $50,000 and reduce the number of tax brackets.
Eliminate direct fuel taxes, carbon taxes, the Employer Health Tax and tobacco and liquor taxes listed in the policy.
Replace the provincial charitable donation credit with an annual donation refund of up to $1,000.
Cut spending, tie program funding to outcomes and use savings for tax relief and debt repayment.
End PST on private vehicle sales.

items.note: These policy articles are linked by the 2026 platform; their original publication dates are in 2024.

items.summary: Allow private surgery options alongside public health care.

points.text: Legalize private delivery options while retaining public payment for services covered by the public system.
Encourage providers to establish specialized facilities for patients whose needs are better served outside acute hospitals.
Emphasize preventative, primary and long-term care.
Use competition between health care providers to reform service delivery and patient access.

items.note: These policy articles are linked by the 2026 platform; their original publication dates are in 2024.

items.summary: Move decisions toward local school districts and develop a system where funding follows students to parents’ chosen education options.

points.text: Shift decision-making from the Ministry of Education toward local school districts.
Consult education providers on an opt-in system in which public funding follows the student.
Allow parents to direct that funding across an expanded range of education options.

items.note: These policy articles are linked by the 2026 platform; their original publication dates are in 2024. The source does not specify a per-student funding amount or an implementation date.

items.summary: Cut taxes by 25% in every income bracket, including corporate taxes, reduce PST by 2 percentage points and balance the budget within four years.

points.text: Cut taxes by 25% across personal tax brackets and corporate taxes.
Reduce PST by two percentage points.
Balance the budget within four years, aiming for surpluses afterward.
Direct a portion of surpluses to debt repayment.

items.summary: Repeal DRIPA, declare UNDRIP without force in BC and halt voluntary transfers of cash, land and resource control to band governments.

points.text: Repeal DRIPA and declare UNDRIP without force in BC.
Halt voluntary transfers of cash, land and resource control to band governments.
Restore oversight of band spending and end mandatory land acknowledgements in government-funded institutions.
Seek constitutional reforms to the Indian Act and reserve system; these changes extend beyond provincial legislative authority.

items.summary: Allow private care alongside fully funded public care and shift administrative spending toward frontline services.

points.text: Allow private health care alongside fully funded public services.
Redirect administration and human-resources spending to frontline staff and care.
Repeal the Health Professions and Occupations Act.
Use the findings of the Allison Inquiry to inform vaccine protocols.

items.summary: Remove SOGI 123, restore standardized testing and introduce a Parental Bill of Rights.

points.text: Restore standardized testing in reading, writing and mathematics.
Remove SOGI 123 and politicized content from classrooms.
Introduce a Parental Bill of Rights providing informed consent and classroom transparency for parents of minors.

items.summary: Eliminate the Step Code and block municipal rent control programs.

points.text: Eliminate Step Code requirements for buildings.
Block municipal rent control programs.

items.note: The priorities page does not provide a construction target or a costed housing program.

items.summary: End safer supply and drug consumption programs, convert consumption sites to recovery centres and introduce involuntary rehabilitation for severe addiction.

points.text: End safer supply and drug consumption programs.
Cancel new consumption sites and convert existing sites into recovery centres.
Introduce involuntary rehabilitation and housing for severe addiction.
Roll back drug decriminalization programs and increase enforcement against open drug use.
